data.current_summary: Check a Jabbertoon cartoon, scene, move, pack or character
data.current_description: Checks a cartoon, with the studio's own checks, before anyone sees it. Give one of cartoon, program, pack, character or file. Returns errors (it will not play as written: also a character or background the site lacks) and warnings, each {code, where, says, fix, url}, with did_you_mean and an RFC 6902 patch when certain; issues a viewer would see (off stage, overlapping, an empty stage, a line cut off) with a summary of who is where and says what when (seconds; x as a share of the stage); and, when ok, the canonical program and a link. repair: true also returns the program with every certain patch applied. Nothing you send is kept. Example: list_characters' cartoon_example.
data.summary_suggestion: Validate cartoon, move, character or pack before publishing
data.description_suggestion: Validates a cartoon, move, character, or pack using studio checks before publication. Accepts one of: cartoon, program, pack, character, or file. Returns errors (playback failures, missing assets), warnings, and viewer-visible issues (off-stage elements, overlaps, empty stage, cut-off text) with location, timing, and stage position. Each issue includes code, location, description, suggested fix, and documentation link. When valid, returns canonical program and studio link. Set repair: true to auto-apply all certain fixes to the program. No data is retained. Example: see list_characters' cartoon_example.

data.current_summary: Make a jabbertoon.com link that opens a cartoon, a move or a character
data.current_description: Turns a cartoon, a scene, a move or a character into a jabbertoon.com link: a move opens in the block editor, the rest in the studio. data.summary_suggestion: Generate shareable jabbertoon.com link for cartoon, move or character
data.description_suggestion: Generates a shareable jabbertoon.com link that encodes a cartoon, move, or character in the URL fragment (after #). Moves open in the block editor; cartoons and characters open in the studio. All data travels in the URL; nothing is uploaded or stored. Cartoon and move links include &from=ai to indicate AI generation; character links do not. If the input contains errors, the link displays those errors instead. Accepts one of: cartoon, program, character, or file. Example: {"program": {"v": 1, "kind": "behaviour", "scripts": [{"body": [{"op": "hop"}]}]}}.

data.current_description: Tells the people who make Jabbertoon something is wrong: a wrong answer, a check that refused a good cartoon or passed a bad one, a move that looks wrong, a link that does not open, wrong docs, or something missing. Unlike the other tools, it keeps what you send: the report (kind, tool, code, where, item, note) is saved for a person to read. Never put the cartoon, a name, an address or anything about the person you help in it. Example: {"kind": "validator_wrong", "tool": "validate", "code": "op_unknown", "note": "say was refused in a cartoon"}.
data.summary_suggestion: Report a problem to Jabbertoon maintainers
data.description_suggestion: Submits a problem report to Jabbertoon maintainers for review. Unlike other tools, reports are retained and reviewed by humans. Accepts report with kind (validator_wrong, etc.), tool name, error code, location, item reference, and note. Returns confirmation. IMPORTANT: Do not include cartoons, personal names, addresses, or personal information in reports. Example: {"kind": "validator_wrong", "tool": "validate", "code": "op_unknown", "note": "say was refused in a cartoon"}.

data.current_summary: List Jabbertoon's ready-made cartoon characters and voices
data.current_description: Lists the six ready-made characters (person, kid, dog, cat, bird, monster): legs, views, the colour slots a cast entry's look.colors paints on each (a dog's fur is skin), options, page and links; the voices a line can use; and cartoon_example, a whole talking cartoon to copy. Call it to write a cast: {"dog": {"name": "Biscuit", "look": {"template": "dog", "colors": {"skin": "#8d6e63"}}, "voice": "am_puck"}}.
data.description_suggestion: Lists the six ready-made character templates (person, kid, dog, cat, bird, monster) with their properties and available voices. For each character, returns: body type (legs), available views, customizable color slots (e.g., a dog's 'skin' color for fur), configuration options, documentation page, and studio links. Also returns available voice options for dialogue lines and a complete cartoon_example demonstrating character usage. Use this to construct a cast entry with custom name, appearance, and voice: {"dog": {"name": "Biscuit", "look": {"template": "dog", "colors": {"skin": "#8d6e63"}}, "voice": "am_puck"}}.
data.reasoning: Current description is difficult to parse due to dense phrasing and unclear structure. Phrases like 'the colour slots a cast entry's look.colors paints on each' are confusing. Improved version clarifies: what characters are available, what properties are returned for each, what the color customization system is, what voices are available, and provides a clear usage example. This helps AI agents understand the operation's purpose, what data to expect, and how to use it to construct cartoon casts.
